newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - Jan 26.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - Jan 26.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Bangladesh press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina is likely to visit India in the middle of next month to inaugurate the inter-parliamentary union conference, beginning in New Delhi on February 14.
Overseas donors are excpected to meet with government officials sometimes at the end of next month to review Bangladesh's progress on economic and institutional reforms.
At least three people, including a minor child, were roasted alive in a fire that raged through a slum in the Dhaka's Khilgaon area at around midnight on Saturday.
Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina on Saturday said that her Awami League government would make all efforts to meet the basic needs of the poor people.
One person was killed and 15 others were injured as villagers in northern Rajshahi district fought with guns and spears over fertiliser price hike.
An Indian national who was imprisoned in Rajshahi jail died of chest pain at the hospital on Friday.

Commerce and Industries Minister Tofael Ahmed leaves Dhaka on Sunday for Brussels to meet the European Union officials amid threats of discontinuation of Generalised System of Preferences (GSP) facility to Bangladesh's garments exports.
Poor handloom weavers will be provided with working capital under a Taka 500 million micro credit programme due to be launched by April.
